Hi Sofia / Liam —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned on performance SLOs and what we’ll validate in the tech deep-dive: 

Recap:
- Primary user flow: clinical note generation in the browser (SSE streaming to web clients)
- Target TTFT (time-to-first-token): P95 <= 200ms (goal: 120–160ms) for single-turn prompts (~128 tokens avg)
- Streaming cadence: client prefers SSE; target chunk cadence 150–250ms, max 400ms between chunks for interactive UX
- Throughput & concurrency: steady-state ~60 req/s, expected peak bursts up to 250 req/s; ~120 concurrent active streams during peak
- Context length: typical 4k tokens, with occasional 16k sessions for long patient histories

What we need from your side to scope the benchmark:
1) One or two representative request payloads (prompt + context) — samples are helpful
2) A short network trace during a representative session (just headers/timings) — you mentioned you can share this
3) Confirmation of SSE vs WebSocket preference (we’ll bench both if you want)

Attached: redwood-ttft-worksheet.xlsx — I filled initial assumptions; please update with exact payload sizes if available.

Next steps:
- You share the traces/payloads (Sofia) — we’ll run an internal baseline perf test against the proposed model variants and quantization profiles
- Schedule 60m deep-dive with our Solutions Engineer + SRE to validate network/topology and run a short live perf run (10–15 min)

Proposed times: Tue/Wed next week 10:00–12:00 PT — let me know what works and I’ll lock in Marissa and our SE.

Thanks,

Thanks for the clear recap, Aditya — very helpful. A couple clarifications and details from our side: 

Clarifications:
- TTFT: our product PM is asking for P95 <= 200ms for the first token across our primary web clients. If you can hit 120–160ms that would be ideal and give us cushion.
- Typical request size: prompt ~200–400 bytes, context ~3k–4k tokens for most cases; long-history sessions up to 16k tokens are rare but critical to support.
- Concurrency/throughput: baseline 50–70 req/s during clinic hours, peaks up to ~250 req/s for batch triage spikes. Concurrent active streaming sessions: ~100–150.
- Streaming transport: browser clients prefer SSE for simplicity; we do have a small set of native apps that use WebSocket. Prioritize SSE for the first pass.
- Chunk cadence: goal is 150–250ms between chunks for perceived responsiveness. We can tolerate up to 400ms occasionally but prefer tighter cadence.

I attached a short network trace (acme-network-trace-20280329.txt) and a sample payload. Can you confirm:
- Do you have recommendations on model family vs TTFT tradeoffs (e.g., 7B quantized vs 13B)?
- For SSE, are there specific keepalive/heartbeat recommendations to avoid intermediaries closing connections?

We’re available Wed 03/30 10:00–12:00 PT or Thu 03/31 9:00–11:00 PT for the deep-dive.

Best,
Sofia
Product Lead, Clinical AI | Acme Health
sofia@acmehealth.com

Sofia — great details, thanks for the trace and sample. Quick answers and what we’ll validate in the bench: 

Short answers:
- Model family tradeoffs: for your TTFT targets we typically recommend a two-path approach: a smaller low-latency variant (7B quantized CPU/GPU-optimized) for interactive flows and a higher-capacity 13B+ variant for high-quality long-history runs. We’ll benchmark both and quantify TTFT/throughput differences.
- SSE best practices: 15–30s application-level keepalive (simple comment/ping frame) and short connection-level timeouts on edge proxies. We’ll provide recommended nginx / CDN keepalive config in the tech call.
- Chunk cadence: we can tune chunk size vs cadence in the runtime; starting point for the bench: aim for 150ms cadence, allow spikes to 400ms under load.

What we’ll run for the initial bench (after you confirm sample payloads):
1) Baseline single-client TTFT for both model variants (cold start and warm cache)
2) Streaming cadence test (SSE) at increasing concurrency levels: 10, 50, 100, 150 concurrent streams
3) Throughput ramp: sustained 60 req/s and burst to 250 req/s to observe tail latencies
4) Network sensitivity: repeat tests with 50–200ms added client RTT to mirror remote clinics

I’ve updated the attached worksheet with the bench plan and initial assumptions (redwood-ttft-worksheet.xlsx). If we’re aligned I’ll schedule the 60m deep-dive and reserve 30m for a short 10–15m live run during that session.

I’m holding Wed 03/30 10:00–11:30 PT — does that work? If so I’ll lock Marissa (our Solutions Engineer) and our SRE.

Thanks,
